fact: The Ministry of Technology, Communication and Innovation, at a working session with Meta in Ebene on 7 October 2026, discussed proposed amendments to the existing Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021, which it treats as the operating legal framework for online content.
The National Crime Agency Bill text published by the National Assembly defines cybercrime by reference to offences under Part III of the existing Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021.

The Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021 (Act No. 16 of 2021) was passed by the National Assembly on 19 November 2021, assented to on 24 November 2021 and gazetted as Legal Supplement 567; the document's retrieval note says it was proclaimed in force on 10 December 2021, and it repeals the Computer Misuse and Cybercrime Act.
Minister Avinash Ramtohul said the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act would be reviewed to address certain offences while strengthening protection of freedom of expression.

ICT Minister Avinash Ramtohul said the existing Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act defines a fake profile, bans its use to cause harm on pain of 20 years' imprisonment and a one million rupee fine, and obliges platform administrators to moderate misleading content.
The Director of Public Prosecutions' April 2024 newsletter cites the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021 as the law under which obscene deepfakes made with intent to harm carry criminal penalties.
The Ministry of ICT's sovereign cloud RFI names the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act (CCA) 2021 among the local regulatory compliance standards suppliers are to implement.
Le Mauricien reports Mauritius's Cybercrime Unit handled 930 cases from January 2023 to January 2026, leading to 130 arrests, with 7 cases referred to court and no conviction yet.

Le Mauricien reports the Cybercrime Unit's count of 930 cases handled between January 2023 and January 2026, with their outcomes (177 closed, 660 under investigation, 33 awaiting DPP advice, 7 before court).
The Prime Minister said the Cybercrime Unit handled 837 cases from January 2023 to November 2025, with 120 people arrested and five cases sent to court, and no conviction yet.
The Prime Minister gave a count of 837 cases handled by the Cybercrime Unit between January 2023 and November 2025, including 167 closed, 640 under investigation and 21 awaiting the DPP.
The Government Gazette publishes the Critical Information Infrastructure Designation Regulations 2026 under the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021, in operation from 1 June 2026.

Minister Ramtohul announced that the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021 is being reviewed to revise definitions and add social media aspects, with a three-month sensitisation campaign before the revised law comes into force.
The Mauritius Prime Minister told the National Assembly that the Ministry of IT is preparing amendments to the existing Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act.

Cabinet agreed on 23 May 2025 to amendments to the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021 through the introduction of a new Bill addressing hate speech, trolling, cyber bullying and disinformation on social media.
The Minister said the planned cybersecurity agency builds on the existing Cybercrime and Cybersecurity Act.
